ADSM401 Group Project As per given due date This assignment must be done a GROUP . Each group consists of 5 members (no more and no less unless specific permission is given by lecturer). Similarity in Turnitin must be less than or equal to 15% or this assignment will receive a mark of 0% or as per policy of DUT plagiarism policy . Turnitin similarity will be done be lecturer. Each student must sign the anti - plagiarism statement or this assignment will receive a mark of 0% . Upload the assignm ent and anti - plagiarism statement to their appropriate Moodle assignment portals. Late assignments will not be accepted. All assignments must be submitted on Moodle wall. On Moodle wall, there will be an assignment portal, where you submit your assignment in MS - Word format, and a plagiarism portal, where you submit a signed anti - plagiarism state ment Assignments must be named with the file naming convention: studentnumber_lastname_firstname_assignmentnumber. All replies will be sent to the student DUT email account. This is for security reasons. Each point should NOT be just listed but include a proper explanation and analysis with full referencing. Referencing does not just mean a bibliography but proper in - text source referencing. DUT policy will be applied if this is not done. Page length is 25 pages, font size 12 with single - spacing. Attempts to “pad” an assignment with carriage returns or poor presentation will be penalized. Pharmaceutical Company BioSynth Solutions has developed a series of modular, automated "Clean - Room Pods" for the production of high - value synthetic vaccines. These pods are designed to operate with minimal human intervention to prevent contamination. Your team must design the software a rchitecture to manage these pods, ensuring that the delicate biological synthesis process is never compromised. System Requirements: • Environmental Monitoring: The system must continuously track: o Air Purity (Particle Count): Using laser counters to ensure I SO Class 5 cleanliness. o Differential Air Pressure: To ensure air always flows out of the pod (preventing contaminants from entering). o Incubation Temperature: Precise to within 0.1 ∘ C . o CO2 and O2 Levels: Critical for the "breath" of the synthetic cultures. o V ibration Levels: To ensure delicate molecular bonding isn't disrupted. • Automated Control: The system must autonomously manage: o HEPA Filtration Fans: Adjusting speeds to maintain pressure and purity. o Precision Heaters/Chillers: Maintaining the incubation thermal "envelope." o Gas Injection Valves: Regulating the atmospheric mix. o Agitators: Controlling the speed of the bioreactor mixing blades.
• Production "Protocols": Users define "Synthesis Protocols" (equivalent to recipes). These specify the environmental setpoints for different phases (e.g., Inoculation, Growth, Harvesting). • Remote Monitoring and Control: Bio - technicians and Quality Assurance (QA) officers must monitor live telemetry via encrypted tablets and a web - based command center. They must be able t o "Pause" a protocol if they see a visual anomaly via the internal cameras. • Fault Detection and Alerting: Any breach in air pressure or a temperature deviation must trigger an "Immediate Containment" protocol and notify the "Sterility Response Team" via SM S and sirens. • Data Logging and Compliance: To meet medical regulations, every second of data must be "Immutable" (logged and unchangeable) for auditing. • User Management: Roles include Lab Technician (Daily ops), QA Auditor (Report viewing), and System Admi n (Managing pods and permissions). • Hardware Integration: Interface with high - precision sensors, PLC - driven valves, and industrial air handling units. • Scalability: The software must handle a single experimental pod or a factory floor containing 100+ pods. Tasks: For this scenario, your team has full creative freedom to determine the internal logic of the system, provided you can justify your choices in the final documentation. 1. Use Case Diagram 15% • Goal: Identify your actors and their goals. • Requirement: You must decide how the "Sensor System" acts as an actor and which use cases are "automated" versus "human - initiated." • Justification: Why did you choose these specific actors? How do they interact to ensure vaccine safety? 2. Class Diagram 20% • Goal: Model the "things" in your system. • Requirement: Choose your own classes, attributes, and methods. • Justification: Explain your choice of relationships. For example, why did you use Composition instead of Aggregation for the relationship between the Pod and its S ensors? Why is a certain attribute private? 3. Sequence Diagrams 20% • Goal: Map the timing of events. • Task A: Create a sequence for a "Critical Threshold Violation" (e.g., the temperature drops too low). • Task B: Create a sequence for "Starting a New Synthes is Protocol."
• Justification: Why does the "Database" or "Actuator" appear at that specific point in the sequence? Why is the user involved (or not involved) in these steps? 4. Activity Diagram 15% • Goal: Map the "Logic Gates." • Task A: Create a workflow for "Sterility Validation" (the checks the system does before it allows a protocol to start). • Task B: Create an activity diagram for "Handling an Alert." • Justification: Why did you place a "Decision Diamond" at that specific step? What happens if a check fails ? 5. Component Diagram 15% • Goal: Map the high - level architecture. • Requirement: Define your software components (e.g., "Compliance Engine," "Hardware Driver Layer") and how they connect. • Justification: Why is one component dependent on another? How does your design ensure that the "User Interface" doesn't directly interfere with the "Safety Logic"? Te c hnical Justification: Quality of the written defence for architectural choices and mapping of requirements to your design 15% Documentation Requirements: Your final submission must include the five diagrams, plus a section where you defend your architecture. For every major class, relationship, or sequence choice, you must explain how it directly addresses the Biosecurity and Precision needs of the BioSynth pods. What needs to be included in the document: UML Diagrams: All five UML diagrams (use case, class, sequence, activity, component) in a clear and well - organized format (e.g., using a UML diagramming tool such as draw.io Documentation: A compr ehensive document that includes: • A description of the scenario and system requirements. • A detailed explanation of each UML diagram, justifying the design choices. • A description of the assumptions made during the design process. • An explanation of how the de sign meets each system requirement. • Acknowledgement by ALL team members of the contribution of each team member
What I will be grading on: Accuracy and completeness of the UML diagrams. Clarity and conciseness of the documentation. Justification of design choices. Demonstration of understanding of UML concepts. Quality of the presentation. Teamwork and individual contributions. Important Notes: Ensure that the diagrams are consistent and follow UML standards. Pay attention to detail and provide clear explanations. Focus on designing a robust and scalable architecture. Use appropriate tools for diagram creation and documentation. Clearly document assumptions and limitations. Demonstrate clear understanding of object - oriented concepts. This assignment is designed to test your ability to apply UML modeling techniques to a complex real - world problem.
